name: weighted opportunity rating combines two ratios at their declared weights (executed-result parity)
description: WOPR is a WEIGHTED SUM OF TWO RATIOS, which one numerator and one denominator cannot express -- which is why it lived in three independently maintained SQL strings until the four-accumulator conversion. Seed one cohort of two receivers over five team targets whose TARGET share and AIR YARDS share disagree in shape: player A takes 1 of 5 targets carrying 30 of 50 air yards, player B takes 4 of 5 carrying 20 of 50. A = 1.5*(1/5) + 0.7*(30/50) = 0.72 and B = 1.5*(4/5) + 0.7*(20/50) = 1.48. The shares are deliberately ASYMMETRIC about one half: with a symmetric split, transposing the two weights merely PERMUTES the two players' values and the comparison -- which is order-insensitive -- stays green over the transposition it exists to catch. Here the transposed pair is {1.04, 1.16}, a different multiset. Also pins the absence of a percentage scale: a 100.0 anywhere in the combine renders 72.00 instead of 0.72.
